html:
The presidential election of 2000, in which the opposition leader Abdoulaye Wade defeated President Abdou Diouf in a runoff on 19 March, ending forty years of Socialist Party rule.

Diouf, president since Senghor stepped down in 1981, accepted defeat and phoned his rival, a rare scene in Africa then. Senegal has since had more peaceful changes: Wade lost to Macky Sall in 2012, and in 2024, after Sall tried to delay the vote, the young opposition candidate Bassirou Diomaye Faye won in the first round. Senegal is one of the few West African states never to have had a coup. See also Dakar.
sum: The presidential election of 2000, in which the opposition leader Abdoulaye Wade defeated President Abdou Diouf in a runoff on 19 March, ending forty years of Socialist Party rule.
